name: Question 15
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14046771/assets/33e48fa5bdbb034bcf489e038ccf80fc5f67baabeccacc1b7abd741183ebf05d.png)

Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x=u-v,\,y=u(u-{v}^{3}).
$$

Which of the following is the image of the side ${S}_{1}$ under the action of $T?$
worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the side ${S}_{1}.$

For the side ${S}_{1},$ we have $v=0$ and $0\le u\le 1.$ Substituting $v=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(u-v,\,u(u-{v}^{3})) \\  & =(u-0,\,u(u-{0}^{3})) \\  & =(u,\,{u}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the image of ${S}_{1}$ can be parametrized by

$$
x=u,\,y={u}^{2},\,0\le u\le 1.
$$

 

Writing this in the usual notation, we have

$$
x(t)=t,\,y(t)={t}^{2},\,0\le t\le 1.
$$

These are parametric equations of a parabolic arc. Notice that if we eliminate $t$ from the equations, we get

$$
{x}^{2}=y\,⇒\,y={x}^{2}
$$

which is a upward-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(0,0).$

Moreover, the endpoints of ${S}_{1}$ are mapped to the $xy$-plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & T:(0,0)\to (0-0,\,0(0-{0}^{3}))=(0,0) \\  & T:(1,0)\to (1-0,\,1(1-{0}^{3}))=(1,1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the image of ${S}_{1}$ is an arc of a upward-opening parabola, traversed from $(0,0)$ to $(1,1).$

Question 15
?

Consider the square region Δ in the uv-plane, given by Δ={(u,v):0≤u≤1,0≤v≤1},

and the transformation T, given by T:(u,v)→(x(u,v),y(u,v)), where x=u−v,y=u(u−v3).

Which of the following is the image of the side S1 under the action of T?

a
An arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from (0,0) to (1,1).
b
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from (1,1) to (0,0).
c
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from (0,0) to (1,1).
d
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from (1,0) to (0,1).
e
An arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from (0,1) to (1,0).
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To map the entire region Δ onto the xy-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the side S1.

For the side S1, we have v=0 and 0≤u≤1. Substituting v=0 into our transformation equations, we obtain (x,y)=T(u,v)=(u−v,u(u−v3))=(u−0,u(u−03))=(u,u2).

So, the image of S1 can be parametrized by x=u,y=u2,0≤u≤1.

Writing this in the usual notation, we have x(t)=t,y(t)=t2,0≤t≤1.

These are parametric equations of a parabolic arc. Notice that if we eliminate t from the equations, we get x2=y⇒y=x2 which is a upward-opening parabola whose vertex is at (0,0).

Moreover, the endpoints of S1 are mapped to the xy-plane as follows:

T:(0,0)→(0−0,0(0−03))=(0,0)T:(1,0)→(1−0,1(1−03))=(1,1)

Therefore, the image of S1 is an arc of a upward-opening parabola, traversed from (0,0) to (1,1).
